title: 1. Zeus, Metis and the succession story
note: Theogony lines 886–900 support the warning, swallowing and counsellor passage; earlier sections describe Ouranos and Kronos. Athena’s armed emergence is described more fully in Homeric Hymn 28, also in the linked volume. The text cannot establish how every ancient listener understood the story. Greek dictionaries give both indicating/telling and, in the middle voice, considering/devising: “closer to point out” is a translation judgement, not a settled correction of Evelyn-White.

title: 6. OpenAI’s charter and the limits of the analogy
note: The charter defines the organisation’s AGI ambition and intended beneficiaries. It does not establish a consensus test for achieving AGI. The extract’s comparison between company control and Zeus is an argument, not a claim that mythological and contemporary arrangements are identical. Assertions about what most researchers accept, or millions of simultaneous conversations, would need separate evidence to be read as measured facts.

links.label: OpenAI Charter

title: 7. The Pile, Gutenberg and Books3
note: The Pile paper documents 22 constituent datasets and an 825 GiB corpus, described approximately as 800GB in its title. The repository includes Gutenberg (PG-19) and Books3. Gutenberg’s possession of a book does not by itself prove that book was in the PG-19 subset or in a particular commercial model’s training data. The Rights Alliance documents its 2023 Books3 takedown work. Next-word prediction is a simplified description: language models normally predict tokens, which need not be whole words.

title: 8. Čapek and the word robot
note: R.U.R. was written in 1920; the play’s ending leaves Alquist alive. Karel Čapek attributed the word to his brother Josef in his 1933 essay. The succession comparison is the author’s interpretation of these works.

title: 9. What the experiments show
note: Berglund and colleagues studied out-of-context reasoning using specially prepared training descriptions. Palisade studied resistance to shutdown during tasks. Neither establishes that reading Hesiod, Frankenstein or stories of rebellion causes real-world AI rebellion. The extract’s suggestion about inherited stories is a hypothesis. Its broad claims about “all” stories and the absence of findings across all research cannot be established by these studies.

title: 10. The Roman heir
note: Roman inheritance could include the deceased’s debts as well as assets. This varied with the kind of heir and period: under Justinian, completing an inventory could limit liability. The final sentence is a compressed introduction to the book’s next section, rather than an account of every Roman inheritance rule.
